messages:
alex: Heads-up — this morning we had ENI/IP exhaustion in eu-west-2 when Karpenter spun up ~120 GPU nodes for large inference batches. Pods Pending with 'no IPs available'. infra-bot sent alert.

infra-bot: [ALERT] subnet-mlpool-eu-west-2a nearing /28 capacity (2 IPs left) — 2026-03-17 08:12 UTC

maria: ugh. same subnet has our batch gpu node pool. Any quick mitigation? :thinking:

sam: short term: scale down low-priority jobs, move some workloads to other AZs or regions. also can taint GPU node template to prefer instances with higher ENI limits (c6i vs g4dn etc.).

alex: tried setting nodeSelector to prefer c6gn.* but GPUs are on p4/gn5. Problem is ENI limits on p4 family are low vs pod density. Karpenter created many small nodes causing more ENIs.

jin: we should consider consolidation: set consolidation.enabled=true and set maxPodsPerNode higher for GPU nodes so fewer nodes are launched. Karpenter consolidation works but default constraints for GPUs kept spread.

maria: worry: raising maxPods may hurt per-pod latency and will need device-plugin / MPS config for multiple containers per GPU. Also driver compatibility.

sam: for network: enable ENI trunking on Nitro instances and prefer trunking-friendly families; increase subnet size (move to /24) but that's infra-heavy. Alternative: use AWS VPC CNI secondary IPs + custom IPAM, or Cilium host-local IPAM.

alex: patch suggestion (short term): 1) bump kubelet maxPods on GPU AMI 2) Provisioner with consolidation + requirements to prefer instance types that support trunking 3) spin up warm standby in another AZ for burst.

maria: can you paste the provisioner patch?

alex: ```yaml
apiVersion: karpenter.sh/v1alpha5
kind: Provisioner
metadata:
  name: ml-gpu
spec:
  requirements:
  - key: karpenter.k8s.aws/instance-family
    operator: In
    values: [g5,p4d,p4de] # prefer families with better ENI/trunking profiles
  consolidation:
    enabled: true
  limits:
    resources:
      cpu: "2000"
  provider:
    subnetSelector:
      karpenter.sh/discovery: eu-west-2
    securityGroupSelector:
      karpenter.sh/discovery: shared
```

jin: also add a startup hook to annotate subnets on the provisioner so Karpenter spreads across all available subnets instead of burning one. We can use topology.kubernetes.io/zone and karpenter.sh/subnet-id annotations.

sam: long-term: request larger CIDR blocks for ML tier (move ML subnets to /22), adopt IPv6 dual-stack for pod IPs (still experimental), or shift to instance types with higher ENI attachments so one node holds many pods.

maria: cost tradeoffs: larger subnets + bigger instances = higher per-node cost but fewer nodes -> lower control plane churn and fewer ENI allocations. We should model GPU utilization vs ENI-related overhead.

alex: action items: @maria run cost model for 3 options (subnet resize, instance-family shift, consolidation with higher maxPods). @jin add provisioner patch to staging and enable consolidation. @sam prepare a short runbook for manual scale-down of low-priority jobs and cross-AZ warm standby steps. I'll monitor alerts and pause new batch submissions if needed.

infra-bot: [NOTE] created incident INC-2026-1984 and tagged eng-infra. Link: https://ops.example.com/inc/INC-2026-1984

maria: ack, starting numbers. :thumbsup:

sam: will do runbook, include kubectl drain snippet and recommended PodDisruptionBudget settings.

alex: thanks team — hoping consolidation + preferring trunking types buys time before subnet resize.
